title: AI-powered Monitoring of Mangrove Biomass and Carbon Stocks
summary: data354 plans AI maps of mangrove biomass and carbon in Côte d’Ivoire; its October 2025 paper derives biomass from 300 field plots and lists the maps as future work.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Pilots in Fresco and Sassandra, Côte d’Ivoire, combine radar, optical, and lidar imagery with 300 ground-truth inventory plots, which the team measured from January to May 2025. In its submission of June 2025, the team says that the system produces monitoring outputs for conservation and carbon accounting, with expansion toward Senegal. The submission does not quantify a restoration effect or a resulting carbon-market transaction. The team released its 300 field plots as an open dataset on 2 October 2025. Its accompanying paper derives biomass from allometric equations and lists the machine-learning maps as future work. On 28 May 2026 the team opened a code repository for CarbonLens, a platform for AI carbon-stock maps of Senegal.
purpose: Improve mangrove biomass and carbon-stock monitoring.
system: AI-powered Monitoring of Mangrove Biomass and Carbon Stocks
location: Fresco and Sassandra, Côte d’Ivoire; Senegal (expansion)

ratings.reason: The makers' own paper of October 2025 states that the AI maps were still future work, and the realized output is a field dataset with biomass from allometric equations. No AI benefit to conservation users is reported.
Restoration and carbon-market benefits are prospective effects of maps that had not been produced.

evidence.citation: Salomon Kouassi, Fabrice Zapfack, Therence Temfack, Gabriel Fonlladosa and Zana Kone (data354), The First Open Dataset of Mangrove Above- and Belowground Biomass and Soil Carbon Stocks in Côte d'Ivoire: Insights from Fresco and Sassandra, Hugging Face and Figshare (doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.30258772), 2 October 2025. The authors are the project team, funded by Lacuna Fund; the dataset and its paper show that the field plots exist and that biomass came from allometric equations, while the machine-learning maps remained future work.
